frontier.hypothesis: The global.c prune_preferences route to target's blocked-but-unallocated $a1/$a2 (inherited from s7) is closed by construction in a two-parameter leaf, and should be proven closed rather than searched further.
frontier.mechanism: regs_someone_prefers[A] is the union of hard_reg_full_preferences over lower-priority conflicting allocnos, and hard-register preferences are created only by copies to or from those hard registers. In a leaf with no call, the only copy touching $a1 is the a1 parameter home itself — and prune_preferences explicitly subtracts an allocno's OWN preferences (global.c:893-895, s2 H7), so the home allocno can never be denied $a1 this way. The route therefore requires a SECOND pseudo derived from a1 that outranks the home copy in allocno_order, and s6 H23 measured that a plain `s32 t = a1;` is copy-propagated away before allocation so no second pseudo exists.
frontier.next_probe: Search for a consumer shape that keeps two DISTINCT a1-derived pseudos simultaneously live (e.g. the value reaching D_80101E7C via a different expression than the one keeping a1 alive) and dump cc1 -da to check whether two allocnos appear; if none can be constructed without a dead value, write the prune_preferences route up as CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION and stop re-opening it.
